title: Headings Practice 8: Language, Learning and Communication
topic: How people learn, speak and share information

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: Children usually acquire their first language without formal teaching. By the age of one they recognise the sounds of their parents' speech, and by two many are combining words. Remarkably, they make systematic errors, such as saying goed instead of went, which shows that they are discovering rules rather than simply repeating what they hear. Adults rarely correct these mistakes explicitly, yet children correct themselves in time.
options: The first words spoken by babies
Evidence that children discover grammatical rules for themselves
questions.answer: Evidence that children discover grammatical rules for themselves
questions.why: Ý chính: lỗi có hệ thống chứng tỏ trẻ tự khám phá quy tắc. Các lựa chọn khác quá rộng hoặc lệch.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: Spaced repetition improves learning by reviewing material at increasing intervals. Instead of studying a list of words for three hours the night before a test, a learner revisits it after a day, then after three days, then after a week. Each recall strengthens memory, and difficult items appear more often. Apps now schedule these reviews automatically.
options: A review schedule that makes memory last longer
questions.answer: A review schedule that makes memory last longer
questions.why: Trọng tâm: lặp lại ngắt quãng giúp nhớ lâu. Ứng dụng chỉ là công cụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: Idioms are difficult for learners because their meaning cannot be deduced from the words. To kick the bucket has nothing to do with buckets, and a person who spills the beans reveals a secret rather than clumsy cooking. Teachers advise learning idioms in context, through stories and conversation, because memorising lists seldom helps people use the expressions naturally.
options: Why idioms are hard to learn and how to approach them
questions.answer: Why idioms are hard to learn and how to approach them
questions.why: Đoạn giải thích vì sao thành ngữ khó và cách học. Câu chuyện chỉ là phương pháp được gợi ý.
questions.quote: cannot be deduced from the words

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: Pronunciation varies enormously within English. In some regions, the vowel in bath is long, in others short, and speakers of some dialects drop the letter h. These differences are not mistakes but patterns that reflect history and migration. Linguists point out that no accent is inherently better, although listeners often judge speakers by their way of speaking and may discriminate unfairly.
options: Regional accents as natural variation, with social consequences
questions.answer: Regional accents as natural variation, with social consequences
questions.why: Ý chính: giọng vùng miền là biến thể tự nhiên nhưng có hệ quả xã hội. Âm h chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Reading speed matters less than comprehension. Many readers try to read faster by skimming, but studies show that comprehension falls quickly once speed rises beyond a modest level. A better habit is to preview the structure of a text, pose questions and pause to summarise. Speed then increases naturally as the reader becomes more familiar with the topic.
options: Understanding, not speed, as the key to better reading
questions.answer: Understanding, not speed, as the key to better reading
questions.why: Trọng tâm: hiểu quan trọng hơn tốc độ. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ nắm một ý nhỏ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: The invention of writing allowed knowledge to survive beyond a single lifetime. The earliest known script, cuneiform, began as clay tokens used to count grain and sheep in Mesopotamia, then developed into wedge-shaped marks pressed into tablets. Over centuries these signs came to represent sounds as well as objects, and eventually were used for laws, letters and poems.
options: The development of writing from simple accounting records
questions.answer: The development of writing from simple accounting records
questions.why: Ý chính: chữ viết phát triển từ ghi chép kế toán. Luật và thơ là các dùng về sau.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: Online translation has improved enormously, particularly for common language pairs. Systems trained on billions of sentences produce fluent results, yet errors persist: idioms are rendered literally, tone is lost, and ambiguous words are mistranslated when context is thin. Professional translators now often use machine output as a first draft, and spend their time correcting and polishing it.
options: Language pairs in the internet age
questions.answer: Machine translation: fluent but imperfect
questions.why: Đoạn đánh giá dịch máy: trôi chảy nhưng vẫn lỗi. Thành ngữ chỉ là một loại lỗi.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Body language accompanies speech, but its meaning varies between cultures. A nod means agreement in many countries, but in parts of Bulgaria and Greece it can mean the opposite. Eye contact signals honesty in some places and disrespect in others. Travellers who rely on gestures alone risk misunderstanding, so it is wise to observe local habits before assuming a meaning.
options: The importance of nodding in conversation
Cultural differences in the meaning of gestures
questions.answer: Cultural differences in the meaning of gestures
questions.why: Ý chính: cử chỉ mang nghĩa khác nhau giữa các nền văn hoá. Gật đầu chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Many students believe they have a single learning style, such as visual or auditory, and that teaching should match it. Yet reviews of the research have found little evidence that matching instruction to preferred style improves results. What does work is matching the method to the content: diagrams for geography, sound for music, practice for skills.
options: Doubts about the idea of fixed learning styles
questions.answer: Doubts about the idea of fixed learning styles
questions.why: Trọng tâm: không có bằng chứng ủng hộ phong cách học cố định. Ví dụ chỉ để minh hoạ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: Public examinations have been criticised for rewarding memory rather than understanding. Candidates sit in silence and write answers to unseen questions within a fixed time. Defenders argue that exams are fair because every candidate faces the same conditions and the marking can be checked. Alternatives, such as portfolios and projects, assess deeper skills, but they are costly to mark and open to unequal help at home.
options: The strengths and weaknesses of examinations as assessment
questions.answer: The strengths and weaknesses of examinations as assessment
questions.why: Đoạn cân nhắc ưu nhược của thi cử. Dự án và chấm điểm chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: Podcasts have grown quickly because they fit into moments when people cannot read, such as driving or washing dishes. Without visuals, the listener forms mental images, which some say creates a more intimate bond with the speaker. Production is cheap, so niche shows on very specific topics flourish; however, finding income is hard for all but the most popular.
options: Why podcasts have become popular and how hard they are to monetise
The cost of making a radio show
questions.answer: Why podcasts have become popular and how hard they are to monetise
questions.why: Ý chính: podcast phổ biến nhưng khó kiếm tiền. Hình ảnh trong đầu chỉ là một lý do.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Literacy rates have risen sharply over the past two centuries. In 1820, only about one in eight adults worldwide could read; today the figure is more than eight in ten. Progress has been fastest where governments expanded free primary schooling and where girls gained access to education. Still, hundreds of millions of adults remain unable to read, two thirds of them women.
options: The history of schooling in the 1820s
Global gains in literacy and the groups still left behind
questions.answer: Global gains in literacy and the groups still left behind
questions.why: Trọng tâm: tỉ lệ biết chữ tăng mạnh nhưng vẫn còn nhóm bị bỏ lại. Giáo dục nữ chỉ là một yếu tố.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Taking notes during a lecture helps learning only if done thoughtfully. Students who try to record everything often write without thinking. Those who listen, identify the main ideas and rewrite them in their own words retain more. Reviewing the notes within a day further strengthens memory, which is why many teachers encourage a short, structured summary after each class.
options: How to take notes that actually improve learning
questions.answer: How to take notes that actually improve learning
questions.why: Ý chính: cách ghi chép hiệu quả. Tóm tắt và ôn trong ngày chỉ là bước phụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Debating teaches more than winning arguments. Participants must research both sides of a question, anticipate objections and respond calmly to criticism. Teachers who have introduced debating clubs report gains in confidence and in the ability to separate evidence from opinion. Some even assign students to defend positions they personally reject, to encourage empathy.
questions.answer: Skills developed through school debating
questions.why: Trọng tâm: kỹ năng rèn qua tranh biện ở trường. Chỉ nhắc một kỹ năng là quá hẹp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Word order differs widely among languages. English places the subject before the verb and the object after; Japanese puts the verb at the end of the sentence; Welsh often begins with the verb. These patterns shape how speakers plan what they say. Learners accustomed to one order often make mistakes in another until the new pattern becomes automatic.
options: How differences in word order affect language learners
questions.answer: How differences in word order affect language learners
questions.why: Ý chính: thứ tự từ khác nhau gây khó cho người học. Mỗi ngôn ngữ chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Newspapers face declining readership as people turn to the internet for news. Advertising income has fallen sharply, leading to newsroom cuts, and in some regions towns have no local paper at all. Some publications have survived by charging for digital subscriptions, while others rely on donations or support from foundations. Many observers worry that less local reporting weakens accountability.
options: The financial crisis of newspapers and what it means for news
Online news sites and their popularity
questions.answer: The financial crisis of newspapers and what it means for news
questions.why: Trọng tâm: khủng hoảng tài chính của báo chí và hệ quả. Quảng cáo chỉ là nguyên nhân.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Calligraphy is regarded as a major art form in China, Japan and the Arab world. Each tradition values the shapes of the letters and the rhythm of the strokes. In East Asia the brush is held upright and the writer moves the whole arm, so that the pressure and speed of every line reveals personality. Students may spend years copying a master before developing a personal style.
options: Calligraphy as an expressive art in several cultures
questions.answer: Calligraphy as an expressive art in several cultures
questions.why: Ý chính: thư pháp là nghệ thuật biểu đạt ở nhiều nền văn hoá. Cách cầm bút và học viên chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: The rise of emoji has changed informal writing. Small pictures convey tone that plain text cannot, softening a request or signalling a joke. Linguists note that emoji function more like gestures than words, and that their meaning shifts depending on age and community. Misunderstandings occur when the same symbol carries a friendly meaning for one group and a sarcastic one for another.
options: Emoji as a replacement for tone and gesture, with risks
The history of pictures in writing
questions.answer: Emoji as a replacement for tone and gesture, with risks
questions.why: Trọng tâm: biểu tượng cảm xúc thay cho giọng điệu và cử chỉ nhưng dễ hiểu lầm. Từng lựa chọn khác chỉ nắm một ý.
questions.quote: function more like gestures than words

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: A dictionary does not decide what is correct; it records how words are used. Lexicographers search large collections of texts to discover which meanings are current, and add entries when a word has appeared often enough over several years. Words that were once condemned as slang, such as mob or sham, now appear without comment, showing how acceptable usage shifts.
options: How dictionaries record changes in word use
questions.answer: How dictionaries record changes in word use
questions.why: Ý chính: từ điển ghi lại cách dùng từ chứ không quy định. Từ lóng chỉ là ví dụ.
questions.quote: it records how words are used

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Storytelling is a powerful teaching tool. Facts embedded in a narrative are easier to remember than the same facts in a list, because listeners follow cause and effect and form emotional connections with characters. Teachers who turn historical events into stories report that pupils recall dates and names for longer. The risk is that the story may become more memorable than its accuracy, so teachers need to check details carefully.
options: Why stories help learning, and the risk of inaccuracy
questions.answer: Why stories help learning, and the risk of inaccuracy
questions.why: Trọng tâm: kể chuyện giúp học nhưng có nguy cơ sai lệch. Lịch sử chỉ là ví dụ.
questions.quote: easier to remember than the same facts in a list
